entries.message: fell back to a client render. This container's server markup was discarded and rebuilt (its template begins {template}; its SSR <style> is kept), so the page is correct but the server's work on it was wasted.
entries.fix: Its children are taken as server output of this template — if they were a client-side placeholder instead, empty the container first (`container.replaceChildren()`) or render the placeholder with vera. Otherwise the two renders have to agree exactly: check for markup the template does not describe, or state settled after the server render. Other containers on the page hydrate independently and are unaffected.

entries.message: there is no renderer to hydrate.
entries.fix: Wire it after the renderer: `wire([renderer, hydration])`.

entries.message: this @verajs/renderer and this hydration are from different releases. Pages render fresh (correct, without adopting the server's markup).
this page was server-rendered with light-DOM slots, which hydration reads through `hydrateSlots`. The server markup is left as served.

`dangerouslySetInnerHTML` is not available on a tag component and has been dropped. A tag binds through `spread`, whose names are only known at runtime — so it refuses `.innerHTML` outright rather than open an unreviewable HTML sink.
entries.fix: Write the element directly, with the value sanitized first: html`<${Tag} .innerHTML=${trusted}>` (see the renderer README's security note).

entries.message: only another tag may be interpolated — a string cannot become markup.
entries.fix: Interpolate a tag: tag`${Base}-card`, where Base is itself a tag.

entries.message: `key` does nothing on a tag component and has been dropped — a key marks a template for list reconciliation, and this call returns one rather than being one.
entries.fix: In JSX, write it and the compiler handles it: `<Row key=${id}>` becomes `keyed(id, Row({…}))`. Calling by hand, wrap it yourself: `keyed(id, Row({…}))`.

entries.message: {text} is not an element name. A tag names ONE element — letters, then letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-' — and nothing else becomes markup here.
entries.fix: Attributes and content belong in the template: html`<${heading} class="title">…</${heading}>`.

entries.message: a tag (`{tag}`) may only stand in tag position — `<${T}>…</${T}>`.
entries.fix: Spliced anywhere else it would become text or part of an attribute, which a tag never means.

entries.message: `style` expects a STRING (e.g. style: `color:${c}`), not an object — as in Vera JSX.
<{tag}> is a void element — it takes no children, and these would be dropped.
entries.fix: Remove the children, or use an element that takes content.
